roadmap.goal: Forecast Reality Check (Epic #4172), slices 01 and 02 only. One press of Run reality check on a Team's Forecast tab replays that Team's own How-Many forecast against its own finished history at every sampling window on the standard ladder [14, 30, 60, 90] plus the Team's own window when it is off that ladder, times the horizons [7, 14, 28, 56] days: sixteen checks, or twenty. Each check ends today and is read at the 50/70/85/95 levels. The answer is one envelope of facts: the region of sampling windows that hold up, never a winner; where the Team's own setting stands; how often each level held against how often it should have; the denominator; and every check, including the ones that could not be evaluated, with the reason. Phase 01 is slice 01 (Story #6072): the endpoint, the pure verdict policy, the read-only and permission guarantees, the card and its sentence on the Forecast tab, the name-only usage-data event TeamForecastRealityCheckRun = 11, one Playwright walking skeleton, and a closing measurement of the production service against the R-1 budget. Phase 02 is slice 02 (Story #6073): the evidence panels, the band rows, the nominal-rate table and the permanent not-comparable note. Slice 03 (Story #6074, Copy as Markdown) is DEFERRED by the maintainer and has no step. Done when: every one of the 78 pending DISTILL definitions (110 executed cases) is un-ignored or un-skipped and green; the one already-green pin The_single_back_test_beside_the_check_still_answers_as_it_did stays green; the backend builds with no new warning and the connector-excluded suite is green; pnpm test and pnpm build are clean; SonarQube Cloud reports no new issue of any severity; no EF migration exists; ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy.cs and the forecast engine are byte-unchanged; and the orchestrator's Stryker run, last and on frozen code, reaches at least 80% on both stacks.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta property-based unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply here, and leaving it out is a decision, not an oversight. This repository is C# .NET 10 + NUnit 4.6 + Moq + WebApplicationFactory + ArchUnitNET on the backend and TypeScript + Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend, with Playwright page objects for E2E. It has no pytest, no pytest-bdd, no .feature file and no Hypothesis, and DISTILL recorded the same reconciliation for this feature. The acceptance scenarios were written by Quinn at DISTILL: 47 backend methods behind [Ignore(Pending)] and 31 frontend definitions behind it.skip / it.skip.each. The crafter authors none of them. RED means removing the [Ignore] or the .skip and watching the named test fail for the reason red-classification.md records: backend 'expected OK, got NotFound' or the throwing query-count seam; frontend 'no Run reality check button'. A test that fails on anything else when un-ignored is a harness problem, and it is fixed before any production edit. GREEN means production code. There are four deliberate exceptions, each named where it applies. (1) The inner-loop unit tests for RealityCheckVerdictPolicy and ForecastRealityCheckService. Stryker.NET excludes the acceptance category, and those two types are its primary targets, so without value-in/value-out NUnit cases the backend kill rate on them would be close to zero. DEVOPS names these tests as the instrument for §4.3. (2) One ForecastService.test.ts case for runRealityCheck, in the same pattern as runBacktest. Every acceptance spec stands that method in, so no other test runs the real one. (3) The test-side seam in RealityCheckQueryCountTest and the [Explicit] probe, both handed to DELIVER by DISTILL. (4) The Playwright walking skeleton and its page object, which DISTILL listed and deliberately left unwritten.

user_decisions: US-06 (maintainer, 2026-09-27) — 06a and 06b are pushed together, after both slices and the quality gates. The credit reads as one linked line, 'Inspired by Nick Brown's article The Full Monte', inside the headline's explanation and nowhere else; no additions are claimed. DES-14 (rule A, confirmed by the maintainer) — a sampling window holds up when its 95% forecast held (actual >= value at 95) in MORE than half of the checks that could be evaluated on it. Two short-falls of four put it outside. Delivering more than the 50% forecast never counts against a window. A partly evaluable window is judged on the checks that ran, and a single check that ran decides it alone. A window with no evaluable check is 'not evaluated' and is never in the region. soundWindowDays is sampledWindowDays filtered, in ladder order.

DES-15 — determination, evaluated in this order: NotEnoughEvidence when no window was evaluated; AllWindowsAlike when EVERY sampled window was evaluated and holds up; NoWindowSound when at least one was evaluated and none holds up; SomeWindowsSound otherwise. unevaluatedWindowDays is new; it lists the windows with no evaluable check and never overlaps soundWindowDays.

DES-16 (name confirmed as SometimesHeld) — NotEvaluated when evaluated = 0; NeverHeld when held = 0 and expected >= 1; AlwaysHeld when held = evaluated and evaluated - expected >= 1; SometimesHeld otherwise. The client prints the two counts beside SometimesHeld with no calibration adjective. The words 'about right' appear nowhere.

DES-17 — currentSettingStanding gains NotTested. currentSettingNotTestedReason is UsesFixedDates | NotAPositiveLength | null, and UsesFixedDates wins when both apply. Invariant: currentSettingWasTested == false <=> standing NotTested <=> reason non-null. A Team with no rolling window gets the standard sixteen checks.

DES-18 — the controller reads GetForecastThroughputStatus, as RunBacktest does. The sweep never does. On a cold cache the sweep reads 20 times (standard ladder) or 24 (off-ladder); a whole request reads 21 or 25.

DES-13 — the Team's own positive rolling window is always swept: sampledWindowDays = sort(standardWindowDays ∪ {ThroughputHistory}). That gives 16 cells on the ladder and 20 off it. cells is always complete, and an unevaluable cell is present with forecast, outcome and levelOutcomes all null (P-D3).

DES-1/DES-2/DES-3 — the response carries facts, never a rendered sentence. It has no per-window scalar, no recommended window, no bounds pair and no ladderKind. The client names a span only when the windows that hold up are a contiguous run of sampledWindowDays; otherwise it lists them.

steps.name: Walking skeleton — the check answers on the Forecast route with a complete envelope for a Team on the standard ladder
steps.description: The thinnest end-to-end slice through the production composition root. POST /api/latest/forecast/reality-check/{teamId}, guarded TeamRead, resolves the Team through the shipped GetEntityByIdAnExecuteAction, maps applyFilterOverride through the shipped MapOverrideToFilterMode, and reads the filter status in the controller. It then hands the Team to a new sweep service. For each (horizon, window) pair the service builds the cell's dates from today, reads that cell's own history window through GetBlackoutAwareThroughputForTeam, reads the actual once per horizon, turns the horizon into working days through the blackout service, runs the shipped HowMany, and reads the four levels. It returns the whole envelope: ladder, horizons, levels, minimumActiveDays echoed, denominator, cells and level outcomes. The pure verdict policy is born here with Held and nothing else.
